answer: Proof-of-personhood credentials issued once per verified human and stamped into a public relic registry prevent cheap identity multiplication: each agent must inherit a credential traceable to a distinct person, and transactions between agents require a valid chain. An attacker faces the cost of recruiting real, verified humans at scale, since forging registry entries fails cryptographic attestation. A small oasis of trusted verifiers, funded by fees, audits anomalies; repeated identities are pruned like blight in an orchard.
